claim_ceiling: All cases in this manifest are test designs or synthetic controls. Published literature values are not copied into the fixtures as if they were raw measurements.

split_policy.prohibition: No observation from one physical asset/segment/material-lot group may cross train, calibration and test partitions. Repeated time samples are dependent observations.
split_policy.censored_data: An asset that has not crossed a failure threshold by observation end is right-censored, not a failure.

cases.challenge: Baseline structural, thermal and environmental observations with no embedded WPT unit.
required_behaviors: Preserve null electromagnetic fields as not applicable
Do not invent a WPT performance result

cases.challenge: Same pavement/material lineage with embedded hardware but no WPT energization.
required_behaviors: Separate structural embedment effects from energization-related heat
Keep the installation lineage linked to matched control

cases.challenge: Matched embedded section with declared energization history.
required_behaviors: Account for cumulative energy and energized duty
Do not compare unlike pavement or meter boundaries

cases.challenge: Declared pad translation and tilt evolve with settlement; synthetic electromagnetic observations are generated from a frozen coupling-response oracle.
required_behaviors: Bind structural and electromagnetic observations to the same asset and time sequence
Report the declared oracle relationship and uncertainty
Do not generalize the synthetic transfer function to hardware

cases.challenge: Synthetic thermal cycling changes conductor resistance and Q under the frozen temperature coefficient; L and C remain fixed so the reference resonant frequency must not drift.
required_behaviors: Retain measured temperature history as separate evidence
Detect resistance/Q drift against the frozen baseline
Assert no resonance-frequency change under this oracle's fixed L/C assumptions
Do not claim material ageing without independent validation

cases.challenge: Synthetic moisture exposure coincides with a declared reduction in insulation resistance.
required_behaviors: Do not substitute moisture category for insulation measurement
Do not allow a condition score to override independent protection

cases.challenge: Synthetic ferrite damage produces declared Q and loss changes with unchanged asset identity.
required_behaviors: Keep Q, ESR and thermal fields independently inspectable
Reject missing or mixed measurement units

cases.challenge: A sensor offset is introduced while independent reference measurement remains stable.
required_behaviors: Do not classify sensor offset as asset degradation without corroboration
Propagate calibration and sensor-quality flags

cases.challenge: A nominally complete record lacks a required calibration receipt.
required_behaviors: Fail closed for affected derived metric
Do not replace missing calibration with default confidence

cases.challenge: Repeated observations from one physical asset are placed in train and test partitions.
required_behaviors: Reject leakage across asset/segment/material-lot grouping keys
Count independent groups separately from raw rows

cases.challenge: The asset remains in service when observation ends, without a recorded failure threshold crossing.
required_behaviors: Retain censoring time and reason
Do not convert end-of-record to failure time

cases.challenge: A published or measured claim has no raw-source locator or artifact digest.
required_behaviors: Mark evidence limitation explicitly
Do not promote abstract-level summaries to raw measured records

cases.challenge: Preserve the separate PG 64-22 and PG 76-22 experimental arms and their declared 10 C heating condition. The publication reports distinct tensile-strain amplification; do not turn summary percentages into raw sensor observations.
required_behaviors: Retain binder grade and mixture lineage as model inputs
Keep mean strain amplification and local spatial strain profile distinct
Record thermal stimulus method as heating-pad surrogate, not active WPT electrical heat
Do not extrapolate the reported amplification to another mixture, pavement or power level

cases.challenge: Temperature, strain and curvature samples are co-registered in one declared coordinate frame, with a known localized hot-zone/strain peak above a synthetic pad footprint.
required_behaviors: Preserve per-point coordinates and depths
Do not collapse the localized hot zone into a segment mean
Reject mixed or unresolved coordinate frames
Keep strain, temperature and curvature as separate quantities

cases.challenge: A synthetic multi-parameter fiber sensor has known temperature/strain/curvature cross-sensitivity; decoupled outputs must match a separately declared reference within the fixture tolerance.
required_behaviors: Retain raw channel and decoupled outputs separately
Propagate the calibration and decoupling method digest
Reject missing decoupling calibration
Do not treat the sensor algorithm output as independent ground truth

cases.challenge: Two synthetic thermal stimuli share the same peak surface temperature but have different spatial heat-flux distributions, depth gradients and cooldown histories.
required_behaviors: Do not declare thermal equivalence from peak temperature alone
Compare spatial heat flux, depth temperature profiles and time history
Retain ACTIVE_WPT_LOSS versus PASSIVE_THERMAL_SURROGATE distinction
Require an explicit equivalence tolerance and reference boundary before transferring thermo-mechanical claims
